newsitem.title: INDIA: India's "Bandit Queen" to surrender, face trial.
newsitem.headline: India's "Bandit Queen" to surrender, face trial.

text.p: Former "Bandit Queen" Phoolan Devi promised on Friday to surrender to a court in northern India to stand trial on a number of charges including the mass murder of her alleged rapists, her lawyers said.
The lawyers told the Supreme Court Devi, now a member of parliament, would surrender on Tuesday before a judge in the northern industrial town of Kanpur.
The Kanpur judge recently issued warrants for her re-arrest to face trial in 57 pending cases, including murder.
In Friday's decision, the Supreme Court rejected Devi's plea to transfer all the cases against her for trial in a Delhi court.
Earlier this month, the Supreme Court rejected Devi's plea for protection against arrest, paving the way for her trial.

Devi, who belongs to the low-caste Mallah community of boatmen, shot to notoriety after 22 upper-caste men were killed in a massacre at Behmai village, near Kanpur in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh in 1981.
She was accused of leading a gang in the massacre but she denied the charges. Devi surrendered to the police in 1983 under a special amnesty offered by the central state of Madhya Pradesh.
Devi spent more than 10 years in prison before being released in 1994.
Movie maker Sekhar Kapoor portrayed Devi as a low-caste heroine in the biographical film "Bandit Queen".
Devi, who is illiterate, was elected to parliament as a member of the Samajwadi Party of Defence Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav, a socialist party of low-caste Hindus, in general elections last year.
